newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caribbean wants more U.S. investment in tourism.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean wants more U.S. investment in tourism.

text.p: The Caribbean Community (Caricom) wants the United States to offer incentives to companies to invest in tourism in the region, officials said on Wednesday.

Bahamian Prime Minister Hubert Ingraham, speaking at the 14-member Caricom summit at the Jamaican resort of Montego Bay, said the incentives could encourage more large U.S. hotel chains to invest in the Caribbean.

Ingraham told a press briefing he was spearheading the effort for "a tourism version of the Caribbean Basin Initiative," which provides preferential access to the United States for Caribbean-made products.
The Caribbean has lacked top-line hotels, he said. Many companies managed properties "but very few of them actually own the properties they manage."
Tourism is the largest single industry in the region. According to the Caribbean Tourism Organisation, gross earnings last year were $13 billion and the United States is the region's largest market.

"With tourism, the Caribbean states for the first time find themselves in the extremely advantageous position of becoming important players in the world's largest employer and fastest-growing industry -- tourism," Ingraham said. "And we boast that the Caribbean is the most desirable 'brand name' in global tourism."
